reference_frame_and_datum.position_eci_m: Earth-centered inertial (EI) axes for each anonymized simulation. The archived t=0 states place +X radial-outward, +Y east, and +Z north at the equatorial launch site; the axes are treated as inertial thereafter. This orientation is inferred from the outputs and is not a published GCRF alignment.
reference_frame_and_datum.velocity_eci_m_s: Earth-centered inertial velocity in the corresponding EI axes; not Earth-fixed velocity.
reference_frame_and_datum.eci_frame_axes: +X radial-outward, +Y east, +Z north at the equatorial launch site at t=0; inferred from archived outputs and not a published GCRF alignment.
reference_frame_and_datum.euler_ned_*_deg: Body attitude relative to local geodetic NED axes; yaw, pitch, roll order
reference_frame_and_datum.body_rate_wrt_ei_*_rad_s: Body components of angular rate relative to Earth inertial axes; roll, pitch, yaw order
reference_frame_and_datum.scenario_initial_body_rate: Zero relative to the rotating launch site, as specified by the model-package input description
reference_frame_and_datum.reference_initial_body_rate: A t=0 trajectory-output sample in the EI frame; not a scenario input

source.citation: NASA Engineering and Safety Center, NESC-RP-12-00770, Check-Cases for Verification of 6-Degree-of-Freedom Flight Vehicle Simulations, Volume II: Appendices, Appendix B.1.6 and C.1.20

extraction.reference_sample_rule: For each anonymized simulation CSV, retain source samples at integer seconds 0 through 200 without interpolation; convert source imperial units to SI with stated exact conversion constants.
extraction.model_normalization: Verify original DAVE-ML SHA-256 values, then strip trailing spaces/tabs and normalize line endings to LF; retain original and packaged hashes separately.

limitations: The source describes an unpublished conceptual rocket model; its aero data are noted as V-2-at-Mach-3 inspired and other values have no further attribution.
NASA Case 17 is a numerical inter-tool verification case, not a flown vehicle or real-world launch event.

The model-package README and report disagree on initial velocity magnitude and direction: the report gives 0.32808399 ft/s (0.1 m/s) upward, while the README gives 0.1 ft/s along body X; the report's upward component matches the archived trajectories.
The scenario's initial body rates are zero relative to the rotating launch site; stored WrtEi rate histories include Earth rotation.
NASA Table 16 and twostage_inertia.dml disagree on yaw inertia; the simulator follows the DAVE-ML equation and retains the printed table values separately.
Atmospheric density, pressure, temperature, Mach and dynamic pressure are excluded from cross-tool comparison above 86 km.
The specified center of mass begins at sea level, so the conceptual vehicle geometry overlaps the ground.
The published source says a 0.001 s step is recommended and the case is sensitive to staging and rotational inertia assumptions.
NASA reports inter-tool differences including 21.6 ft position difference at 200 s for one 1000 Hz comparison and much larger deviation for an alternate inertia model.
The reference CSVs are anonymized simulation outputs; they are not treated as a single truth trajectory.

source_discrepancies.report_value: 0.32808399 ft/s upward relative to the launch site (0.1 m/s)
source_discrepancies.selected_basis: Volume II, Appendices, pp. 34 and 68; the selected upward 0.1 m/s component is corroborated by the three trajectory CSVs

source_discrepancies.scenario_value: zero relative to the rotating launch site
source_discrepancies.selected_basis: Volume II, Appendices, p. 68 for initial conditions and p. 56 for output-frame definitions

source_discrepancies.detail: SIM 6 retains nonzero atmospheric fields above 86 km; NASA excludes these channels from Case 17 comparison
The vehicle center of mass starts at sea level, placing the lower vehicle below the surface

source_discrepancies.report_value: Table 16 lists Izz equal to Ixx
source_discrepancies.model_value: twostage_inertia.dml computes Izz equal to Iyy
source_discrepancies.selected_basis: The simulator follows the explicit DAVE-ML output equation; both values are retained

source_discrepancies.report_value: Greater than 125 km for the specified rotating Earth
source_discrepancies.archived_history_check: All three terminal 200 s ECI vectors have below-surface two-body perigees under the recorded Earth constants
source_discrepancies.resolution: Unresolved; the report's perigee frame, epoch, or gravity convention is not identified by the archived output CSVs.

terminal_two_body_conic.interpretation: All archived terminal ECI vectors produce below-surface osculating two-body perigees under these constants, contrary to the report's greater-than-125-km statement. The source's perigee frame/time/gravity convention is unresolved.
